ceiling_when_clear_of_walls.why: trade practice: a device the plan draws clear of every wall (no wall face within 2 ft of its symbol) cannot be on a wall; a luminaire, exit sign, sensor, detector, speaker or antenna there hangs from the ceiling over it (a switch, receptacle, thermostat, outlet, pull station or duct detector never does: it is on a wall or in its duct). One whose documents say wall goes on the ceiling only when its schedule, legend or type also allows a ceiling (CEILING/VARIES)

defaults.why: the usual height of a switch (48" to its middle), no document gives one
the usual height of a thermostat (48" to its middle), no document gives one
the usual height of an equipment connection, no document gives one
the usual height of a wall fire alarm appliance (80"), no document gives one
the usual height of a door holder, no document gives one
trade practice: a wall-switch (switch-box) occupancy sensor takes the switch's place in its box at the door: a switch's height (48" to its middle), no document gives one
the usual height of a wall occupancy sensor, no document gives one
the usual height of a wall cleanout, no document gives one
the usual rim height of a lavatory or sink (34"), no document gives one
trade practice: a washer outlet box sits above the washer, its standpipe 18 to 42 inches over its trap (IPC 802.4.3): 42" to its middle, no document gives one
trade practice: a hose bibb or wall hydrant 18 to 24 inches over the floor or grade (24"), no document gives one
the usual height of a wall faucet or eyewash, no document gives one
trade practice: an expansion tank hangs on the water heater's cold supply above the heater (72" to its middle), no document gives one
trade practice: a valve on the water heater or supply piping is set where it can be reached and serviced (60" to its middle), no document gives one
the usual height of a wall plumbing connection, no document gives one

trade practice: a luminaire built into casework is most often a task light under the upper cabinet, whose underside is 54" over the floor (a 36" counter and 18" to the cabinet): its top there, no document gives one (the alternatives, a toe-kick or display light, take their detail's height)
the usual height of a receptacle or device (18" to its middle), no document gives one
